name: Agent inventory entry
purpose: One record per agent in a dedicated agent inventory, separate from the model inventory. The underlying model is registered there as a vendor model with a version. This entry is the source of truth for the autonomy tier, and the tier drives everything downstream.
when: At intake. Updated on any change of tier, owner, model or status.
where: Inventory service with an API. The CI pipeline and identity issuer read it.
fields: status: proposed | pilot | live | suspended | retired
done_when: The pipeline selects the control profile from this tier, and an agent with no inventory entry cannot be issued a workload identity.
metric: Inventory coverage = agents holding a live identity that are also in the inventory ÷ all agents holding a live identity (target 100%)
note: Tier vocabulary from IMDA §2.1.1 autonomy spectrum.

references.why: Risk from impact factors (domain, data, external access, scope, reversibility) × likelihood factors (autonomy, task complexity, exposure)
Autonomy tier per agent in a dedicated inventory; promotion as a governed event

name: Agent justification record
purpose: Explains why this needs an agent rather than a rules engine, a process fix or a scorecard. It is written before funding, in the terms the benefit will later be measured in, and includes the permanent cost of outcome sampling.
when: Before funding. Revisited whenever the benefit case changes.
where: Business case template, as a mandatory section.
fields: alternatives: deterministic rule · process change · scorecard, and why rejected
benefit in analyst hours & cycle time
cost of sampling loop (09) per year
consequence class of a wrong decision
done_when: Someone who disagrees with using an agent can see which alternative was rejected and on what numbers, and the sampling cost is on the benefit line rather than discovered in year two.
metric: Sampling cost present in business case (Y/N). Realised vs claimed benefit at 12 months.
note: Renamed from 'agency justification record' to avoid the banking and government sense of 'agency'.

references.why: Determine suitable use cases for agent deployment
Intended purpose and context; potential benefits; potential costs
Objectives for responsible use; intended use

name: Third-party evidence pack
purpose: Collects the evidence behind every control a model vendor or agent platform claims to handle. A claim is an assertion until evidence is attached. Per the source reference, a 2026 index of 30 deployed agentic systems found only 4 publish a safety system card and 25 disclose no internal safety results.
when: Opened at intake, complete before G3, refreshed on vendor change.
where: Supplier file, linked from 06 component definitions.
fields: evidence per claim: test report | attestation | certification + scope
contract: no training on data · log export · audit rights · incident notice
record export the organisation can chain & sample (SaaS)
done_when: No control in 06 is marked 'inherited from platform' without evidence attached.
note: Open question: where the gate lives when the agent is vendor SaaS.

references.why: Responsibilities outside the organisation: model providers, platforms, tool hosts

references.source: SG Govt ICT&SS Policy, GenAI SSP
references.why: Legally binding commitment that the provider doesn't log, store or train on data

name: Delegation policy (the mandate)
purpose: The most important document in the set. It states what the agent may decide alone, what it must escalate, whose authority it acts under, what it may read and touch, how it is assured, and what ends it. It expresses authority as a tier, not a yes or no. The accountable executive countersigns the tier and the tolerance.
when: Before build. Re-approved on every tier change and every material change.
where: YAML in the agent's repository. The policy gate is compiled from it, with no hand configuration.
fields: auto-decide scope: case types, value limits, jurisdictions
assurance: control profile, sampling rate & floor, tolerance
done_when: The policy gate can be configured from this document with no interpretation, and a supervisor can read it and say which tier the agent sits at.
metric: Gate-config drift = diff(compiled 02, running gate policy). Must be 0.
note: Field structure from arXiv 2607.17225. Tier from IMDA §2.1.1.
example:
# 02 · delegation policy · illustrative
agent: sanctions-triage-l1
purpose: dispose first-line name-screening alerts
authority:
  tier: T3                      # agent operates, human approves exceptions
  auto_close:
    alert_types: [name_match]
    max_match_score: 0.82
    excluded_jurisdictions: [comprehensive-sanctions programmes]
    excluded_list_entries: [PEP, adverse-media]
  must_escalate:
    - list_version_changed_since_last_calibration
    - any_field_missing_in_grounds
    - confidence < 0.90          # must point to a row in 10
information:
  may_read: [alert, kyc_record, payment, list_entry]
  may_not_read: [SAR_filings, investigator_notes]
tools: [kyc.read, payment.read, list.read, alert.close, alert.escalate]
assurance:
  controls_profile: tier-3
  sampling: {rate: 3%/month, floor: 300, by: independent-review, blind: true}
  tolerance: {disagreement_max: 2.0%, set_by: accountable_executive}
evolution:
  material_change: [model_version, prompt_hash, tool_manifest_hash, list_format]
  on_material_change: full_sample; calibration_void
sunset: 2027-09-30 unless re-approved

references.why: Bound risks through design (limits, identity, authorisation); significant checkpoints for high-stakes or irreversible actions
Declare what an agent may do before runtime assessment
Roles and responsibilities; processes for responsible use; intended use
Roles for human-AI configurations and oversight
Tool misuse; identity and privilege abuse, bounded by tools and permissions
Human oversight able to override and stop

name: Hazard analysis & failure-mode register
purpose: Records what can go wrong, including failures that emerge from parts interacting rather than parts breaking. Specialists produce it and hand it to the business to challenge. It is not elicited from the business in a workshop.
when: Before requirements. Re-run as a delta on every material change.
where: Risk register, with every hazard linked to control stories (04) and controls (05).
done_when: At least one registered hazard needs two simultaneous conditions to occur. That is the sign the analysis looked at interactions, not just components.
metric: Hazards linked to ≥ 1 tested control ÷ all hazards (target 100%). Count of interaction hazards (≥ 1).
note: Read from four perspectives: the attacker, a supervisor two years from now, operations at 3am, and the person who was wronged.

references.why: Method: control structure, unsafe control actions, loss scenarios

Prompts: goal hijack, tool misuse, identity & privilege abuse, supply chain, unexpected code execution, memory & context poisoning, insecure inter-agent comms, cascading failures, human-agent trust exploitation, rogue agents
Map workflows to exploitation points; rogue actions and sensitive-data disclosure as primary risks
Impact assessment process, documentation, individuals and groups, society

name: Data & context provenance record
purpose: Records what the agent reads, retrieves and remembers: every source, corpus and memory store with its classification, owner and version. Memory and retrieval corpora are attack surface as well as data.
when: Design. Updated when any source, corpus or memory store changes (material change).
done_when: Every item in 02 may_read resolves to a row here with an owner and a classification the hosting is authorised for.
metric: may_read items without a provenance row (target 0).

references.why: Data for development, acquisition, quality, provenance, preparation

references.source: SG Govt ICT&SS Policy, GenAI SSP
references.why: Permitted classification by hosting; self-hosted environment authorisation

name: Control requirements as backlog items
purpose: Each control is written as behaviour with acceptance criteria, in the same backlog as the feature work. Controls are derived from the hazard register and the catalogue, not invented per project. Requirements in a non-functional annex have no owner, estimate, test or demo, and they are the first thing dropped when a date slips.
when: Continuously, in normal refinement. Control stories are demonstrated at sprint review.
where: The team's backlog tool (e.g. Jira), labelled with the control ID and linked to the 03 hazard.
done_when: No control lives in a document the pipeline can't read, and sprint review shows control stories alongside feature stories.
metric: Control stories with an automated acceptance test ÷ all control stories. Control stories deferred vs feature stories deferred per release.
example:
AGT-014  Every autonomous closure carries a decision record
  Given  the agent proposes alert.close
  When   the gate allows it
  Then   a decision record exists before the core system is called,
         with grounds.matched_fields, grounds.dob_delta_days,
         grounds.list_version, grounds.rule_id populated
  Evidence  decision_record_id on the closure event
  Test      count(records) == count(closures), nightly; any gap fails the build

references.why: Why annexed requirements fail: a filing problem, not an elicitation problem
Technical controls during design and development

name: Machine-readable control specification
purpose: The controls expressed as data. Each control carries its applicability, a deterministic test, the evidence it emits and its on-fail action, with one tailored profile per tier so selection becomes a lookup. This is the reusable, organisation-wide asset.
when: Built once, then versioned like code. The profile is selected per agent at every build.
where: OSCAL repository: catalog → profile per tier → mappings.
fields: applies_to: tier, data class, consequence class
maps_to: AICM · ISO 42001 · IMDA · IM8/SSP · AI Act
done_when: The CI/CD pipeline selects the applicable profile from the inventory tier and runs every test without a human interpreting anything.
metric: Applicable controls with a deterministic test (%). Controls passing per agent per build (%).
note: Don't write a house catalogue. The mappings are the asset, and a house catalogue throws them away.

references.clause: 247 objectives, 18 domains; mappings to ISO 42001, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF & 600-1, BSI AIC4, AIUC-1

references.source: SG Govt ICT&SS Policy, GenAI SSP
references.why: Import as a profile for public-sector deployments

references.source: CSA agentic profile · OWASP Agent Control Standard

name: Pre-deployment evaluation report
purpose: Evidence that the agent behaves as the mandate says before real cases reach it. Tests cover whole workflows, not just final outputs, and every escalation condition has a test proving the agent escalates. For T3 and T4, independent review runs or witnesses the evaluation.
when: Before G3, and as a regression suite on every material change.
where: Evaluation harness in CI; report attached to 06. For government, Litmus run IDs are recorded here.
fields: scope: task execution · policy compliance · tool-calling accuracy · robustness
done_when: Every must_escalate condition in 02 has a passing test that proves escalation, and every red-team finding is fixed, accepted by the AOW, or linked to a control.
metric: Escalation conditions with a passing test ÷ all escalation conditions (target 100%).
warning: A test set isn't the production population. 13 is necessary but it can't substitute for 09.

references.why: Test task execution, policy compliance, tool calling, robustness; whole workflows; realistic environments; repeatedly
Pre-deployment safety testing for government AI

name: Agent definition & build attestation
purpose: Describes what this agent is in a form a machine can check, signed at every release, including prompt-only releases. It lets any decision record be resolved to the exact build that made it.
where: Artefact registry, signed. Components expressed as OSCAL component-definitions.
done_when: For any decision record you can name the exact model, prompt and tool set in force, and prove the running build is the approved build.
metric: Version drift = decision records whose triple ≠ attested build (any > 0 is red).

name: Transparency notice & operator guide
purpose: Has two audiences. People affected by the agent are told they are dealing with one, what it can decide, and how to reach a human. Operators get training on the agent's failure modes and on how to approve, override and halt it, because oversight that isn't trained is a rubber stamp.
when: Before G3. Refreshed on material change, and operator refreshers run on a schedule.
where: Published notice; operator guide and training records in the LMS.
fields: operator: failure modes · approve / override / halt · automation-bias training · refresher cadence
done_when: A user can find out, in the channel they are using, that an agent acted and how to reach a person. Every on-the-loop operator's training is current.
metric: Operators with current training (%). Canary catch rate (see §6).

references.why: End-user transparency; users who integrate agents; train humans on failure modes, audit oversight

references.source: SG Govt ICT&SS Policy, GenAI SSP

references.why: Transparency to deployers; oversight persons aware of automation bias

name: Oversight pack & tile register
purpose: The written specification for the dashboard, not the dashboard itself. It is a register of tiles, each labelled Process, Outcome or Unknown, each traced to source records. It is agreed with internal and external audit before go-live and signed by the accountable executive. The monthly pack is generated from it by query.
when: Specified before G3. Generated monthly. Re-signed after every full sampling round.
where: Tile register (versioned document) plus a generated dashboard.
fields: provenance (outcome tiles): population, n, who, period, interval
done_when: No tile can be read as a safety number without saying so, and the accountable executive has signed the register, not just the dashboard.
metric: Pack generated by query without manual steps (Y/N). An Unknown tile is present (Y/N).
note: Rules: every tile states its kind · every outcome tile shows its provenance · tails not means · an Unknown tile is mandatory · business and technical views reconcile to the same records.

references.why: Sufficient, appropriate evidence; agree with audit first

name: Change, incident & decommissioning playbook
purpose: Treats prompt, tool and model changes as material. Incident response is written for actions, not outages. It names a kill-switch owner and a maximum time to halt, and it includes a decommissioning path.
when: Before G3. Drilled on a schedule (quarterly for T3 and T4).
where: Operations runbook, with drill records feeding 11.
fields: incident classes: wrong action · compromise · drift
containment: revoke identity → disable tools at gateway → halt
kill-switch owner, deputy, max time-to-halt, last drill
decommission: records retained, permissions revoked, inventory closed
done_when: The last drill halted the agent inside the stated time, and the record of it is in the oversight pack.
metric: Time to halt (last drill). Drill age. Change-to-revalidation days.

references.why: Supersede, disengage, deactivate; incidents communicated; decommissioning
Define interventions per alert type, from scheduled review to immediate halt; gradual rollout

references.source: PRA SS1/23 · DORA · FSB sound practices

name: Decision record
purpose: One record per action, sealed before execution: inputs read, tools called, action proposed, structured grounds, gate verdict and version triple. It is the direct equivalent of the case file that has to survive inspection years later. A record written afterwards is a different and lesser thing.
when: At the moment of decision, emitted by the platform. Never by a person.
where: Append-only store. JSON canonicalised (RFC 8785), SHA-256 chained, signed, optionally Merkle-anchored per batch.
done_when: A record from eighteen months ago can be pulled, its chain verified, its version triple resolved to the exact artefacts, and its grounds re-checked by a script, with nobody who built the agent in the room.
metric: Record completeness (worst day). Chain verification (records verified ÷ records).

references.clause: Record, hash chain, trust_level, signer_kid, optional ML-DSA-65 & RFC 6962 anchoring

references.why: Trajectory telemetry (development status: pin attribute names)
Records for review, accountability and remediation
What to log: prioritise high-risk actions

name: Control outcome record
purpose: One record shape emitted by every control run. It is dull on purpose, and it is why a single query can answer "every agent in the organisation, status today".
done_when: The oversight pack is generated by query, not assembled by hand, and two teams' agents appear in the same table without translation.
metric: Evidence freshness (age of latest passing result, worst control). Pass rate by agent.

references.why: Approaches to track existing and emergent risks

name: Outcome sampling plan & results
purpose: The only artefact that says anything about whether decisions were right. Reviewers independent of the agent's owner re-perform a stratified random sample of closures, blind to the agent's answer. The result is a disagreement rate with an interval. The method is fixed before the results are known.
when: Monthly. A full round after every material change and before every tier promotion.
where: Sampling tool reading the 07 store. Results emitted as OSCAL assessment-results observations.
fields: strata: confidence band · case type · risk category · jurisdiction
classification: agent wrong · reviewer wrong · both defensible
results: rate + Wilson 95% overall & by stratum, worst stratum
done_when: An examiner can be told the disagreement rate, its interval, its worst category and who found it, and be shown the method was fixed before the results were known.
metric: Disagreement rate (Wilson 95%), overall and worst stratum. Unknown coverage.
note: At T2, human approval of every action already reviews 100%. Still sample the approvals, to detect rubber-stamping.

references.why: Same logic, pointed at the agent's closures
Audit oversight regularly; address automation bias

name: Calibration record
purpose: Required wherever the agent's own confidence decides what is auto-closed. It shows whether the confidence bands mean what they claim, using the 09 results per band. Without it, the routing threshold is an engineer's feel.
when: After a minimum number of sampling rounds (four). Void on any material change.
where: Validation record, referenced by 02's routing threshold.
fields: per band: closures, sampled, disagreements, observed rate + interval
done_when: The auto-close threshold in the mandate (02) points at a row in this record rather than at an engineer's judgement.
metric: Bands calibrated / not calibrated / void. Rounds held.
note: Reduction rule: four consecutive in-tolerance rounds, then a reduced rate with a floor of 300 per band per quarter, reset on material change.

references.why: Performance measured in conditions similar to deployment
